title: Spike a saline bag without touching the sterile spike or port, then prime the drip chamber
instruction: Prepare the hanging IV bag aseptically: remove the blue spike-port cap and the navy giving-set spike cap without touching either exposed sterile interface, turn the drip chamber upright, seat the upward-pointing spike to its collar, keep the chamber axis within 12 degrees of vertical below the port, then squeeze and release until the gravity-referenced liquid height from the outlet end is 15-27 mm. Release everything and return both arms to their starting poses.
context: Spiking an IV bag and setting the drip-chamber level is routine IV preparation for registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00, over 3 million US workers) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061.00, about 0.6 million), done by hand many times a shift. The difficulty is physical: uncap both sterile interfaces and seat the spike axially in a 10 mm port without either exposed end touching anything nonsterile, then squeeze the chamber to a set level.
setup: Fixed YAM station, metres from the arm-base midpoint: x forward, y left, z up (table top at z 0.7475). A nonsterile stainless tray, 34 x 54 x 0.4 cm, covers x 0.16-0.50 and y -0.30-0.24. A sealed 500 mL saline bag (PVC, 13 x 20 x 2.6 cm, 530 g) hangs vertically, ports down, its centre at (0.39,-0.122,0.99), from a fixed IV support (a 60 cm steel pole and a 16 cm backplate whose binder clip holds the bag's top seal, so it hangs still). Its 10 mm spike port ends in a blue pull-off cap with a 12 x 12 x 110 mm printed pull strip. The giving set stands upright, spike up, its chamber centre at (0.36,-0.30,0.8315), in a nonsterile molded cradle: an 80 x 80 x 8 mm base, a 25 x 12 x 56 mm post and a 25 x 26 x 6 mm shelf, whose spring clip lets the set go only when pulled with more than 8 N. Its 20 mm x 45 mm drip chamber wears a clear printed handling sleeve (40 x 20 x 24 mm wings, two 50 x 4 x 35 mm flanges); the set weighs 20 g, tubing and closed roller clamp are visual only. The spike's navy cap has a 12 x 12 x 40 mm printed tab. Both sterile interfaces begin capped. After either cap comes off, its exposed end must not touch any gripper surface (palms, finger shafts or fingertip pads), the tray, the cradle, the IV support or the bag's outside. Priming needs the chamber within 12 degrees of vertical with the outlet end below the inlet and the liquid at least 10 mm below the port.
scoring: Contamination latches 0 for good if, after its cap is off and before the spike locks, the open port mouth or the exposed spike touches any gripper collision surface (palm or either finger, all collision meshes), comes within 0.5 mm of the tray, the cradle, the IV support or the bag's outside, or the chamber overfills above 34 mm. Otherwise, measured at trial end: 0.25 when both protective caps are off (port cap moved 5 mm or more, spike cap 6 mm or more); 0.5 when the spike is also seated 23-25 mm with its collar at the port mouth; 1.0 when the liquid height above the outlet-end graduation, measured vertically, is 15-27 mm with the chamber axis within 12 degrees of vertical, the bag still hanging, both TCPs at least 4 cm from chamber and port and within 5 cm of their starts, and bag and set at rest for 1 s. All other outcomes score the highest completed uncontaminated stage. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Each real trial uses a fresh sealed bag and a fresh sterile giving set; move the printed pull strip, tab and handling sleeve onto them. Hang the bag in the binder clip, ports down; close the roller clamp; push the set into the cradle's clip, spike up, capped. Discard either item if an exposed end touched anything. Use object_jitter=0. Simulation reset restores both cap seals, the rack clip, the contamination latch, the spike joint and the liquid height.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Caps tear off at 3.5 N and 0.08 N; the rack clip breaks at 8 N; the bag hangs fixed. The port grips the spike with about 1.5 N; membrane piercing is not modelled. Contamination is geometric: gripper collision hulls, the tray plane, and every collidable shape of the cradle, support and bag except the port. Liquid is a height proxy from measured squeeze travel, only while seated, upright and below the port; no fluid or chamber deformation is simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 in 1,337 steps
